title: Plural affirmative yes/no questions
summary: Form olemmeko, oletteko, and ovatko questions for plural persons.
objectives: Attach -ko to each plural affirmative form.
Keep plural person agreement inside the question word.
Use oletteko for plural and polite-singular te.

sections.title: Three plural question forms
paragraphs: Begin with the matching plural olla form and add -ko: olemmeko, oletteko, ovatko.
The entire form is one word. It appears before the explicit subject pronoun.

sections.title: Te in a question
paragraphs: Oletteko te can address a group or one person politely. The grammatical form stays plural in both cases.
Use the context to understand the social meaning; use oletteko for the grammar.

steps: The form also fits polite singular te.
Place he after the question verb.

commonMistakes: Do not separate -ko from the verb.
Do not shorten oletteko when addressing one person politely.
Do not pair he with olemmeko.
